chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever breaks the fast for a part of the month of Ramadan due to an excuse, if he makes it up consecutively, that is better; and if he makes it up separately, it is good.
ai.seo_question: Is it better to make up missed Ramadan fasts consecutively or separately?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Ishtibār clarifies the juristic preference (afḍaliyya) for consecutive makeup fasting (qaḍāʾ mutatābiʿ) versus the validity of scattered fasting, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease combined with excellence. It underscores the principle that while continuous fasting is meritorious, breaking it for valid reasons does not invalidate the obligation, aligning with the broader Shia legal tradition of balancing rigor with practicality.
